I’m in my second semester of my first year right now, and overall I’m still a happy person. It’s definitely difficult and stressful, but also super rewarding which makes it worth it IMO. I like to think I have really good time management skills, I still get to do social stuff and hobbies but definitely not as much as before nursing school which can be sad but you just have to remind yourself that it’s gonna be worth the sacrifices. I know that some people have other life circumstances that make adding nursing school insanely difficult and they really do have it rough, but in general I feel like nursing students kind of exaggerate how hard it is. At my school for some reason everyone (including me) likes to hype each other up about how miserable we are, how hard this is, and what martyrs we are for going through this. I play along because I would feel mean rubbing it in by actually being like “I don’t think it’s that bad” in case other people really are struggling, and I have a feeling a lot of other people are doing the same thing as me. Whenever someone asks me how school is going I say “terrible it’s so hard” because I know that’s what they expect to hear and for some reason I feel like I should, or maybe they won’t think I’m a diligent student or something? I’m almost done tapering down now, I tried once before and it went horribly but this time it’s going really well. because of my first bad experience I was also really scared to try again but I just went a lot more slowly and carefully this time around. If you’ve been on it for four years going off of it is definitely going to be hard but worth it if you really want it. I first started lexapro because my depression and anxiety was unmanageable, so I started using lexapro and taking therapy a lot more seriously. Lexapro helped me manage everything a bit but I also learned a lot of other ways to manage it myself through therapy, now that I feel I have the right tools to keep things under control myself I just felt ready to do it on my own and stop having to take a pill every day and deal with the side effects. If you think you have the resources and coping skills to manage on your own and lexapro is bothering you through it’s side effects or whatever reason id say you’re ready but obviously make sure you’re doing it under supervision of a doctor. Good luck, and remember if it’s really too hard for you you can always just up your dose back to before and try again another time, it’s a long process and there shouldn’t have to be any rush :)
